subject: Packaging + Procurement: hosting option & paperflow qualification
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mark Thompson <mark.thompson@acmehealth.com>, Sandy Lee <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Apr 7, 2027 at 4:45 PM -0700
Subject: Packaging + Procurement: hosting option & paperflow qualification

Hi Mark / Sandy —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can align the commercial path before your procurement loop: 

Recap from our conversation:
- Use case: HL7 ingestion + clinical summarization for pilot (non-PHI in initial phase).
- Expected pilot run rate: ~100k generated tokens/week, ramp to steady-state in 3–6 months.
- Technical preference: keep data in-region (US), potentially private deployment later.

Two quick procurement/financial questions to confirm the right pricing packet:
1) Purchase mechanism: do you expect this to be processed via PO (standard for platform purchases) or corporate card for an initial pilot under $10k?
2) Marketplace interest: would you prefer to transact via AWS Marketplace / Azure Marketplace (third-party billing) or direct invoicing from Redwood?
3) Commit discipline: would Acme consider a committed capacity term (3/6/12 months) if the discount profile is attractive, or do you need purely on-demand pricing?

Attached is a short PDF that lays out our three hosting packaging options (Hosted API, Dedicated Reserved Capacity, Private VPC) and the high-level commercial behaviors. Karthik and Marissa are looped in to propose a price/commitment table once we confirm procurement preferences.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm procurement preference (PO vs card) and marketplace appetite.
- If PO: please share any standard PO processing timelines or a purchase-tracking contact.
- If committed: let us know a target commitment horizon (months) and target monthly spend so we can prepare a committed-tier quote.

Thanks — happy to set a 30-min procurement-specific call if that helps.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_Hosting_Pricing_Options_v2.pdf

From: Mark Thompson <mark.thompson@acmehealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sandy Lee <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, Apr 8, 2027 at 9:12 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging + Procurement: hosting option & paperflow qualification

Hi Lauren —

Appreciate the concise recap. A few answers from our side (procurement + finance):

1) Purchase mechanism: For any platform contract we expect a PO and invoice flow. For small pilots <$10k we can use a corporate card, but long-term procurement requires PO-based invoicing and our standard T&C review.
2) Marketplace: Marketplace is attractive from an ops standpoint, but only if it does not complicate our internal PO and invoice reconciliation. Historically, our finance team prefers direct vendor invoicing when we need a single recurring PO. So marketplace is a possibility but not the preferred route.
3) Commit vs on-demand: We are open to a committed arrangement if discounts are meaningful (we typically look for >=25% on committed spend vs list). Otherwise we'll start on on-demand and consider a commit after the pilot if performance and cost profile look good.

Procurement items: I attached our PO workflow and the procurement contact (Sandy) who handles vendor submissions. Our standard commercial security checklist will come through your integrations team if we proceed beyond pilot. Timeline: expect 4–6 weeks for a PO + contract review for a mid-size commercial purchase.

Could Karthik/Marissa provide a short pricing matrix (hosted vs dedicated vs private) showing expected monthly invoice profile for both on-demand and a 12-month commit at a couple of tier levels? If you can include any one-time onboarding fees for Private deployment, that will speed our internal review.

Thanks,
Mark
Director, Digital Platforms | Acme Health
mark.thompson@acmehealth.com

Attachments: Acme_PO_Workflow.pdf

Lauren — looping in. Thanks Mark for the procurement clarity. Action items from our side: 

- I'll build a compact pricing matrix (single-page) that compares: Hosted (on-demand invoiced monthly), Dedicated (3/6/12 month commits with examples for 30/50/70% utilization), Private (one-time onboarding + monthly infra + support).
- Include a column for "Procurement-friendliness" indicating whether each path supports PO/invoice, card, and marketplace.
- Call out data residency considerations for Private (one-time setup and committed infra may be required to meet in-region guarantees).

What I need from Lauren (quick): a target committed monthly spend if Acme is willing to consider a 12-month term, and any redlines in your standard SOW that procurement typically requires (Sandy's PO workflow helps).

I'll also prepare two scenario quotes: (A) pilot (on-demand) estimate and (B) 12-month committed discount example at -30% to show savings. Will attach an XLSX and a one-pager.

Karthik
Head of Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mark Thompson <mark.thompson@acmehealth.com>, Sandy Lee <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Apr 8, 2027 at 10:42 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging + Procurement: hosting option & paperflow qualification

Mark / Sandy —

Thanks — attaching the short one-pager and a draft XLSX price comparison. High level summary here so procurement has a quick decision guide: 

- Hosted (Redwood API, on-demand): No commit required. Invoiced monthly; supports PO for longer relationships and card for pilots. Low onboarding time. Good for exploratory pilots.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): We offer 3 / 6 / 12 month commit options. Typical commercial thresholds: 3-month minimum with modest commit, 12-month gives the deepest discounts. Example: 12-month commit -> ~30–45% off list depending on capacity profile; includes an SLA and higher throughput guarantees. Billed monthly via invoice/PO.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): One-time onboarding and integration fees (typical range $25k–$75k depending on scope) plus monthly infra + support. Procurement will want a SOW + PO for onboarding. Often paired with a committed capacity model.

Marketplace note: We can support AWS Marketplace procurement, but as Mark mentioned, that can complicate PO-level reconciliation. If Acme needs a single recurring PO, direct vendor invoicing is typically cleaner.

Attached files: Acme_OnePager_pricing.xlsx (includes pilot vs 12-month commit rows), Redwood_Hosting_Pricing_Options_v2.pdf (same as previous).

Proposed next steps:
- If PO path: Sandy, can we schedule a 30-min call next week to walk your vendor intake checklist?
- If committed preference: Mark, please suggest a target monthly commitment you want us to model at -30% and we'll send a redline-friendly quote + sample SOW.

Happy to jump on a quick call with procurement to speed the process.

Best,
Lauren
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: Acme_OnePager_pricing.xlsx, Redwood_Hosting_Pricing_Options_v2.pdf

Lauren / Karthik —

Good summary. Procurement preference: PO-based invoice is our default for platform deals. Let's do a 30-min procurement intake on Wednesday 4/14 at 10:00 AM PT (Sandy will send a calendar invite).

On commitment: if Redwood can demonstrate ~30% discount on a 12-month committed profile with monthly invoicing, that's something we can present to finance. Marketplace is low priority for this procurement.

Please include a sample SOW and one-page commitment quote ahead of the procurement call.

Thanks,
Mark
